record.tranche_reason: The author argues that high-activating examples can give a misleading interpretation of a feature across its activations, bearing on V6. The post also reports a manual feature-recurrence tally and a correlation simulation, neither of which tests the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The post discusses Anthropic's SAE features, not neuron poles. Cited findings from Anthropic are not recorded as study results. The Golden Gate feature's activation-distribution estimate is the author's own eyeballing; the median-instance judgment is attributed to Anthropic's autointerpretability metric.
record.test_reason: The post comments on Anthropic's Scaling Monosemanticity SAE work. Its main point is that an SAE feature named from its top examples (Golden Gate Bridge) is irrelevant to that label at most activations. That matches V6's logic, but it concerns SAE dictionary features, not neurons. The share estimate is the author's eyeballing of Anthropic's published histogram, plus Anthropic's own autointerpretability labels, so it is not a new measurement. The feature-recurrence tally and the correlation simulation concern SAE consistency and feature–neuron correlation, not any version. No version is tested on neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author also concludes that Anthropic's ~0.3 maximum feature–neuron correlations are far above chance, contrary to Anthropic's framing that no neuron is strongly correlated. He also notes there is still no gold-standard metric for dictionary quality.
record.recipe_differences: The post uses an author's visual estimate of an SAE feature's activation distribution and a manual comparison of SAE feature lists; it does not reproduce the Qwen neuron-pole audit.
record.method_sensitivity: The Golden Gate interpretation is presented as applying at very high activations, not to most activations.

fits_no_version.finding: Per the author's eyeballing of Anthropic's histogram, the Golden Gate Bridge SAE feature (34M_31164353) is bridge-related only at very high activations, under 10% of its activations. Anthropic's autointerpretability rates the median active instance as irrelevant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features labelled from their top-activating examples are not well described by that label across most of their activation distribution (an SAE-feature analogue of V6).

fits_no_version.finding: Only 7 of 22 listed safety-relevant 1M SAE features had a related 34M feature, by the author's manual tally.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs of different sizes do not consistently recover the same features.

fits_no_version.finding: A random-process simulation gives maximum correlations below 0.02. The author therefore reads Anthropic's ~0.3 feature–neuron correlations as far above chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features are substantially more correlated with individual neurons than chance would predict.

record.problems: The Golden Gate activation share is an eyeballed estimate. The recurrence tally covers only 22 selected safety-relevant features and is manual; the author notes that the list may not be exhaustive. The correlation simulation is not a measurement on the model.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V6 'challenges' label is dropped: the unit is an SAE feature, not a neuron, and the share is a reinterpretation of Anthropic's figure rather than a held-out test. The comments (e.g., Riggs on activation-weighted measures, Burget on non-exhaustive lists) are discussion, not results.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares and tested explanations of neuron poles.
Interpretability shares across language models, architectures, and scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization.
Architecture, regularization, tool quality, and the proposed InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
Attribution graphs using a large model's own neurons and reconstruction error.
The post discusses an SAE feature, not a neuron, and does not run a held-out test of neuron explanations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

rows.locator: A Feature Isn't Its Highest Activating Examples
rows.note: The author says the high-activation instances correspond to the bridge, while a median active instance is irrelevant to it according to Anthropic's autointerpretability metric. The less-than-10% estimate is based on the author's eyeballing, not a reported quantitative test.
rows.check: The subject is an SAE feature, not a neuron, so it does not bear on V6, which concerns neuron explanations. The value is the author's eyeballed reading of Anthropic's figure, and the 'irrelevant at median' judgment is Anthropic's own autointerpretability result, so it is effectively a cited result. Moved to fits_no_version.
